clue.text: I got out from prison amid opprobrium to create cryptic

indicators.note: amid means set in the middle of the other piece, so the prison word sits inside

parts.note: opprobrium is harsh criticism, i.e. abuse

indicators.note: the letter I has got out of the prison word, so it is removed from it

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A prisoner escapes amid public outrage, creating a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like a crossword reference, but here it simply means obscure; 'got out from' and 'amid' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means hard to understand or obscure, which is what cryptic means here.

clue.text: Describes basic act, or elaborate? The latter

definitions.text: Describes basic act, or elaborate? The latter

indicators.note: elaborate means worked out in detail, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a word describes a simple act or a fancy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' rearranges BASIC ACT OR; the whole clue says the answer describes an elaborate act.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatics are gymnastic feats, an elaborate kind of performing act.

clue.text: Siren evident as many in stick-up held by force

indicators.note: held by means the inner piece is gripped inside the force word

parts.note: stress is force or pressure

indicators.note: in means the many letter goes inside the turned stick
in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a cue is a billiards stick
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: A siren appears as several people are held up at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick-up' reads as a robbery but splits: the stick, and 'up' reversing it in a down clue; 'in' and 'held by' are the container indicators, giving EDUC inside the force word.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, like the mythical sirens who lured sailors.

clue.text: Boy, some natural philosopher

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boy is something of a natural philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a common male first name, so it stands for any boy.

clue.text: Peter the 13?

definitions.meaning: Peter ... was a famous British nightclub owner
the answer at 13 is a puppet, a fellow worked on strings

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Stringfellow ran glamorous nightclubs in Britain. Read in two parts, the name also describes a puppet, a fellow on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A string-operated puppet can be jokily called a fellow on strings, and Peter is the clubowner's first name.

clue.text: One demanding much interest in university, more reliable

parts.note: surer means more dependable

explanation.surface: A student loan lender at a university is described as more dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer is a moneylender who charges excessive interest on loans.

clue.text: Possible description of old bloke, one in bed endlessly

definitions.meaning: a dirty old man may be called lecherous or worse
someone who never wants to leave bed, for amorous reasons

explanation.definitionFit: A lecher who always wants sex might be called both a dirty old man and someone forever in bed.

clue.text: Open space brought about for confined one

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a moor is an open expanse of land

explanation.surface: An open space is brought in for a confined person.
explanation.definitionFit: A room is an enclosed space, so a confined one where 'one' stands for space.

clue.text: Smutty and indecent going topless

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: crude means vulgar or indecent

explanation.surface: Smutty, indecent behaviour involving going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' takes the C from CRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean vulgar or sexually suggestive, as in rude jokes.

clue.text: Siren's signal right, altered wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are put together in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning siren's signal has been wrongly changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is an emergency warning, the kind of signal a siren gives.

clue.text: City roundabout to cross by car

parts.note: a roundabout is circular, shaped like the letter O
a cross is the letter X
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Driving round a city roundabout to get across.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is an English university city.

clue.text: Bow with end missing — I sent it to be fixed on time for musician

indicators.note: end missing means the last letter of the actress's name is dropped

parts.note: Clara Bow was the American silent-film star

indicators.note: fixed means repaired, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A violin bow is broken and sent off for repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with end missing' drops the A from CLARA; 'to be fixed' rearranges I SENT IT to INETTIS, then T goes 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinettist is a musician who plays the clarinet.

clue.text: Caught with Charlie in embrace of fertility god, perfect for flipping drunken debauchery

indicators.note: being in the embrace of something means being held inside it

parts.note: Baal is the Canaanite fertility god
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Charlie Chan is the fictional Chinese-American detective

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the perfect word is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Someone is caught with a friend in a god's embrace, at a drunken orgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For flipping' reverses A1, read as AI, to IA; 'flipping' also poses as a mild oath. The detective is the less obvious reading of Charlie, usually C in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchanalia is a drunken orgy, named after the Roman festival of Bacchus.

clue.text: 10-1 about to be carried by horse, "Plaything"

indicators.note: being carried by the horse means sitting inside the horse word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

parts.note: betting odds of 10-1 are read ten to one, with one as the Roman I

explanation.surface: A ten-to-one shot carried by a horse is the favourite plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: Odds of 10-1 are said 'ten to one'; 'about' rearranges TEN TO I into IONETT, and 'to be carried by' puts it inside the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked by strings, which is a plaything.

clue.text: Appear to absorb two articles, one being the main thing

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the articles go inside the verb

parts.note: to appear is to seem
a and an are the indefinite articles
a and an are the indefinite articles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeming to soak up a couple of things, one becomes the most important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic phrase for the sea, so the main thing is a sea creature; 'to absorb' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea anemone is a creature living in the sea, so it is a thing of the main.

clue.text: Pound, half of that loot

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: to loot is to rob

explanation.surface: Half of a pound in stolen loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to beat rhythmically, as a heart or headache can throb.

clue.text: Complaint given audible support gets cut

parts.note: a beef is a complaint

indicators.note: audible says the support word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a stake is a post that props something up

explanation.surface: A grievance gets support when it is voiced, then gets cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefsteak is a slice of beef, so it is a cut of meat.

clue.text: Be unfaithful, when Orient FC a shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leyton Orient FC play badly; a fan feels let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shambles' rearranges ORIENT, FC and A. Leyton Orient is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To fornicate is to have sex outside marriage, which can amount to being unfaithful.

clue.text: Keep governor with tinned lager?

indicators.note: with here joins the container to what it holds; tinned lager is lager inside a tin

parts.note: a tin is a can
Stella Artois is a well-known brand of lager

explanation.surface: A castle governor relaxes with a can of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinned lager is lager inside a can, which is why 'with' can join container and contents. A keep is a castle's central tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the governor of a castle, and a keep is a castle stronghold.

clue.text: Mate with 1.3 billion people?

definitions.meaning: roughly the population of the country in East Asia

explanation.definitionFit: China is Cockney slang for a friend and also the most populous country.

clue.text: Unfairly treat anti-war backbencher, to be put to death in church

parts.note: Clare Short, a Labour MP, resigned from cabinet over the Iraq war and returned to the back benches

indicators.note: in means the execution word is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to hang is to execute

explanation.surface: An anti-war MP is to be executed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A backbencher is an MP without a government post; 'in' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change someone is to cheat them, giving less than is due.

clue.text: Inside which male will be after a quickie!

definitions.text: Inside which male will be after a quickie!

indicators.note: after means the male letter follows the animal

parts.note: a hare is a fast animal, jokily a quick one

explanation.surface: A man is looking forward to a quick fling.
explanation.walkthrough: M comes after HARE; the whole clue describes the women's quarters where a man would go for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a household, where a man might seek sex.

clue.text: Sound of Beagle on final approach to Mars?

definitions.text: Sound of Beagle on final approach to Mars?

parts.words: Sound of Beagle on final approach to Mars?
parts.note: a beagle is a dog, and also the Beagle 2 space probe, which crashed on Mars

explanation.walkthrough: The bark of a dog, and also the noise a crashing probe might make on landing: a pun on Beagle 2, the British probe lost on Mars in 2003.
explanation.definitionFit: A woof is the bark a dog such as a beagle makes.

clue.text: Battle, but no hill side

indicators.note: but no means the hill word is taken away from the battle

parts.note: Edgehill was the first battle of the English Civil War, 1642
taken as written

explanation.surface: A battle fought on the flat, without a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border or side of something.

clue.text: Lots of pampered pooches heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: poodles are dogs often pampered and groomed

explanation.surface: Pampered dogs losing their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes the P from POODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it means lots of.

clue.text: Party animal back on scored lines

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

indicators.note: back means the animal is read in reverse

parts.note: an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: A party animal gets back to the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party animal' poses as one phrase, a reveller, but splits into two pieces; 'back' reverses the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera, the words set to the score.

clue.text: Bizarre nose, but no head, in fish

indicators.note: in places the headless nose inside the fish word

parts.note: fry are young fish

indicators.note: no head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: beak is slang for nose

explanation.surface: A strange fish with a nose but no head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But no head' removes the first letter of the nose word; 'in' puts what is left inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Freaky is informal for weird or strange, which is bizarre.

clue.text: Charge marked on drug

parts.note: stamped means marked with a stamp
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A criminal charge marked on a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush, a charge of animals or people.
